reviews.review: It's a pretty fun game to play with strangers, and really fun to play with friends. As a rabid Aliens fan, I absolutely love it. I loved Colonial Marines though too, even though that was nonsense. Just want to shoot pulse rifles at xenomorphs. I see Aliens franchise, I buy XD.
Definitely better with friends, that is unless your friends are named James.

This game is pretty cool, but I wish it was more replayable and had more content. It's boring to play the same story missions over and over again (the card system doesn't change much about the mission and some of the cards are very irritating) And the horde mode missions only have 3 similar looking maps.

It got very boring very quickly

i started out with pre ordering the standard edition, well after about 3 days i decided to upgrade and get the whole deluxe pack with all the dlc and addons after i saw how they are actively trying to fix bugs, and increase the fun and content of the game. I was extremely hesitant due to the failures of other aliens games but i am happy to report this game is as awesome and addicting as it looks from the previews i saw before its release. i wish teams could be composed of 4 players however that does not subtract from the fun factor at all, i would suggest this game to those that are holding out seeing what other people think of it and happen to like the alien movies, and, those looking for a fun pve game.

Enjoy spending ~20 hours leveling up your characters so you can play the hard difficulties, which is literally what the entire game is building you towards, just to find out you can never find a full match and actually play afterwards. 

Some guy in the reviews here decided to use middle school math to explain how broken the matchmaking system is, but tl;dr there's just no quickmatch or easy join-by-difficulty/campaign/etc... matchmaking system. Instead you have to pick the specific mission, difficulty, cards enabled/disabled, launch and then - the worst part - YOU ONLY HAVE 60 SECONDS OF MATCHMAKING before bots auto-populate your match in the last 20 seconds and force launch it. If you want to play with people (which is needed and most the fun of the game) you have to keep backing out after 40 seconds and searching endlessly in the abyss of this half-brained multiplayer system

Finally using the IP correct and giving us..not the deepest aliens game but a good one none the less.

Fun and easy to pick up.

Playing with friends might be worth a few nights of fun if you spread it out or one good session if you're hardcore. The weapon customization is pretty good too. At the time of writing this review I've sunken about 27 hours into the game, having played in the first month following the game's launch.

At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite is a fun game with friends which captures the spirit of James Cameron's Aliens sequel quite well. At its worst, it's a decent but flawed attempt at the replayable co-op shooter concept popularized by Left 4 Dead.
If you're an Alien fan and you're looking for some fun co-op action then Aliens: Fireteam Elite delivers and you'll get a good 30-ish hours out of it. But if the franchise means little to you, you'll most likely find the game outclassed by other titles in the genre such as Vermintide 2, World War Z  and even the classic Left 4 Dead 2.

I am torn. The game is well worth the money.  I have had tons of fun and think most people should pick it up and enjoy it. If you have friends that want to play, that is.  The current matchmaking mechanic (or lack thereof) is the reason I am not recommending the game.  If they fix this by adding lobbies, quick play, or any other route to meet people and not just say... Keep spamming the mission you want to do on Intense+ and hope more than one person joins within 40 seconds before the AI is added in and people quit.

However, if you want to play a 1-1 simulator over and over again... Grab the game, you should be fine.

Aliens Fireteam Elite had a lot of potential, but ultimately falls flat due to poor gameplay. While the graphics and sound design are impressive and do a great job of creating an atmosphere of tension and dread, the gameplay itself is lackluster and frustrating.

The game's mechanics feel clunky and unresponsive, with poor hit detection and unsatisfying weapon feedback. The AI of the aliens and other enemies is also lacking, with predictable patterns and little to no challenge. And while the variety of weapons and classes is promising, the lack of customization options and the fact that the game quickly becomes repetitive make it difficult to stay engaged.

Another issue with Aliens Fireteam Elite is the lack of content. While there are a few different mission types, the game quickly becomes monotonous as you repeat the same objectives over and over again. And the story, while intriguing on paper, is poorly executed, with flat characters and a predictable plot.

In addition, the game suffers from technical issues and bugs, with frequent crashes and glitches that can disrupt gameplay and lead to frustration.

Overall, while Aliens Fireteam Elite had the potential to be a great co-op shooter, it falls short due to poor gameplay mechanics, lack of content, and technical issues. It's a shame, as the game's graphics and sound design are impressive, but ultimately these positives are outweighed by the frustrating and repetitive gameplay.

If you're an Alien franchise fan, love the second movie (Aliens), and enjoy co-op shooting, then there's really no reason not to give this game a try. Honestly, if you answered yes to all three of the preceding questions, then you'll most likely enjoy Fireteam Elite. It doesn't do anything special or new, but it does have solid game play and the sound, environment and character design all nail the franchise aesthetics extremely well. If they can keep adding content I can see myself revisiting this game fairly often.

First the at release or even with the recently added phalanx class this game is not worth $40.  What you're buying with $40 is the future potential.  

This game reminds me a lot of Warframe when it first came out. (like day one)  Fun but limited and very repeatative.  But warframe was free (and still is) this is not, this is borderline AAA title price

They REALLY need to do something with matchmaking.  It feels like no one plays because each queue is seperate and theres no option for "give me any team on X difficulty"  or "give me any team playing X map"  Without filters theres 100 different matchmaking qeues so often times you end up playing with bots.  

This game really shines when you play it with friends. If you can premake your 3 man squad then its a bunch of fun.

For those complaining about no in game grouping mechanic you can join in on each others games via steam friends but yes, there definitely needs to be some in game grouping system.

Like I said, there's a bunch of potential here but as is they have not delivered on what I paid. If they try and release a bunch of nickle and dime DLC  I'll switch this to a no go because at $40 I expect more and hopefully they will deliver.

That said they have been on top of updates so far, releasing a new class, new weapons etc. so the team is very active which gives me hope.

I have mixed feelings about this game but overall worth my $40.

D.E.D, dead. Truly a game that died after your first play-through. Although this game's core loop is to replay missions in different ways with people on certain difficulties, it gets far too repetitive and the gameplay becomes stale WAY too quick.

if we assume a 5/10 is average, then i'd give it
4 / 10  if playing solo
7 / 10  if playing with friends
8 / 10  in a couple months,   probably

As far as it goes, it works really well as a horde shooter, aliens can crawl along the ceiling and walls and do well to swarm you, sadly though they do have limited amounts of routes they can take to get to you, they all seem to path-find on the same 4-6 routes, so quite often you get lines of enemies from different directions, even if they do break apart as they get closer, this can understandably make it feel repetitive for some. 

The campaign is really nice, but sadly doesn't have a whole lot of replayability on its own, Challenge cards help offset this, either by having some sort of looming threat or by disabling something in your equipment, or maybe just a specific milestone for the mission, these do offer a good trade in difficulty for speeding up the process of using other weapons and getting their passive boosts.

The perk sections are quite refreshing, where you can pick out specific boosts and attach them to abilities, either giving more range, quicker recharge, or special effects,  each class can usually change or effect how one specific ability works as well, you unlock extra sections in your perk grid to add more upgrades the higher you level your class.

Each mission has a hidden cache that can give you extra loot, on top of this you can unlock quite a generous amount of weapons just through your first play through of the game, and even more if you play through the game again at a higher level, the game sort of hinders itself like this though, as you can purchase other weapons, but it doesn't show most if any of the weapons you can unlock through the campaign, so it makes its own weapon arsenal seem smaller then it actually is, same deal with weapon attachments, and you can even find perks as well.

Pros:

Good choice of weapons.

Difficulty really has a good curve to it, and challenge seekers wont likely be disappointed by the higher end stuff.

it has a good progression of enemy types, and certain enemies really require you to focus them down before you're swarmed.
